chunks: By Allah, I had no liking for the caliphate, nor any interest in government,
but you yourselves invited me to it and prepared me for it,
When the caliphate came to me, I kept the Book of Allah in my view and all that Allah had put therein for us, and all that according to which He has commanded us to take decisions; and I followed it,
and also acted on whatever the Prophet - may Allah bless him and his descendants - had laid down as his sunnah.
In this matter I did not need your advice or the advice of anyone else,
nor has there been any order of which I was ignorant so that I ought to have consulted you or my Muslim brethren.
If it were so I would not have turned away from you or from others.
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali not consult Talha and Zubayr in governance?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies that his governance was rooted in the divine text and Prophetic Sunnah rather than political expediency, asserting that his independent judgment (ijtihad) was sufficient and error-free. This response underscores the Shia principle of the Imam's infallibility in religious and political leadership, distinguishing his authority from the advisory role expected of companions like Talha and Zubayr. By citing his adherence to the Quran and Sunnah as self-sufficient, he refutes the claim that excluding them from consultation constituted a breach of protocol.
